case.pattern_description: The pattern consists of a rapid burst of four online purchases of product C, each priced just under the $500 threshold (ranging from $464.46 to $488.58) within a 21-minute window on 24 Nov 2016, affecting the Mastercard debit card C10751-K1. It was identified when an analyst reviewed a device profile (Windows 10, Chrome 63.0) that had been used on multiple cards and flagged a monitor sweep of four sub-threshold transactions on the same card. This sub-threshold burst matches a template seen on 15 other cards in the prior three weeks, leading to a fraud verdict and card block.

evidence.claim: 4 online purchases of $464.46 to $488.58 within 21 minutes, each just under $500; before this burst the card's largest online purchase was $150.00
The same template (three or more online purchases just under $500 within 40 minutes) appears on 15 other cards within three weeks

Model risk score 0.21. For product C transactions with an identity record in this score band, 14% were confirmed fraud in July to October (8,416 transactions), so the score is read at that calibrated rate, not at face value
The device profile was already used by this card 14 time(s) before

Policy applied, Fraud Policy R9: Undocumented patterns: When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST, and describe the pattern in your own words.

Nearest documented pattern by text similarity is Known fraud patterns: Card-not-present fraud (cosine 0.81), which does not describe a coordinated template across customers; its definition: The number is used online without the card.

case.summary: The alert was triggered by a monitor sweep that detected four online purchases just under $500 on card C10751-K1 within 40 minutes. The strongest findings are that four online transactions ranging from $464.46 to $488.58 occurred in a 21-minute burst, a pattern that matches a template seen on fifteen other cards and exceeds the card's previous maximum online purchase of $150.00, while the model risk score of 0.21 is calibrated to a 14 % fraud rate for product C in the same score band and the device profile had been used by this card fourteen times before. The case was judged to be fraud with a probability of 0.92. The recommended actions are to block the card, create a new case, file a report, and escalate the matter to an analyst.

sar.narrative: The cardholder identified by customer ID C10751 and card ID C10751-K1, a Mastercard debit, was the subject of a series of unauthorized online purchases. Four transactions occurred on 2016-11-24, beginning at 17:00 and ending at 17:21, with amounts ranging from $464.46 to $488.58, the flagged transaction (ID 3483895) amounting to $475.22. All purchases were made through the online channel using product code C and were billed to regions 123, 225, and 420. The first three transactions employed three different device profiles: Trident/7.0 on Windows 10 with IE 11, and two instances of Windows 10 with Chrome 63.0; the final three transactions, including the flagged one, used the same Windows 10 Chrome 63.0 profile. The activity was carried out as a rapid burst of online purchases priced just under the $500 threshold, a pattern not documented in known fraud typologies. This pattern is suspicious because the card's prior online purchase history showed a maximum amount of $150.00, and the same template of three or more sub-$500 purchases within 40 minutes has appeared on fifteen other cards in the preceding three weeks. The cardholder has not yet been contacted, and the card was blocked as a containment measure.
